title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan tentang cuaca panas, hujan, dan berangin serta memahami teks tentang cuaca dan pakaian yang sesuai.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 86-87
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to make predictions with “if” and “will / won’t” about the weather and clothing.
Learners will be able to speak and write about clothes, accessories, and the weather using the first conditional (If it’s …, I’ll / I won’t …).
Learners will learn and discuss the importance of good decision-making skills.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
Review the vocabulary from the unit with a quick game: the teacher says a clothing item (e.g. a sun hat, thick gloves, a long raincoat) and students shout out the weather for it (sunny, cold, rainy).
Ask 2-3 students, “What did Laura take with her on the rainy and windy day?” to review the reading text from the previous lesson.
Other alternatives to warm up the class: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 86.
First, the teacher reads the questions in the speech bubble at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the questions aloud as a class.
Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs.
Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary, e.g. “What will you wear if the weather is hot?” → “What will they wear if it’s cold and windy?”

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different things. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.

Highlight the pattern If + present simple, will / won’t + base verb (If it’s cold, I’ll wear a coat. If it’s hot, I won’t wear a sweater.) and the common mistake “If it will be rainy …” (correct: “If it’s rainy …”).
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at Speaking and Writing B on Student Book page 86 and ask some instruction-checking questions.
Read the example aloud together as a class. Also read the questions that they will ask each other.
Put students in pairs. Tell students to ask and answer the questions with their partner, and that the answers must be written in complete sentences.

Remind students to follow the structures shown in the Q&A models and Language Box, and to combine one weather word with two clothing items, e.g. “If it’s hot and sunny tomorrow, I will wear a sun hat and a short-sleeved T-shirt. I won’t wear a thick sweater or waterproof boots.”
Give students around 12-15 minutes to complete the task. Circulate and help students who need support.
Elicit answers from the class. Answers will vary, so show some model answers from the Teacher’s Guide as good examples and correct mistakes together.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Write the following question models on the board:
Q: What will you wear if it’s windy?  A: I’ll wear a jacket and long trousers if it’s windy.
Q: What won’t you wear if it’s windy?  A: I won’t wear a short-sleeved top or a short skirt if it’s windy.
Tell students to change the weather word to ask their partner about different types of weather, using vocabulary from Student Book pages 81 (Vocabulary A), 83 (Listening A), and 84 (Reading A).
Put students in pairs and give them about 6-8 minutes to ask as many questions as they can. Then elicit some answers from the class and give feedback if there are mistakes.
Direct the students to look at the picture on page 87 and ask them “What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.

Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value (Personal Development & Self-Management: good decision-making skills). They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think this skill (or value) is important?”
Read instructions 1-4 of activity A aloud together as a class, and ask some instruction-checking questions.

Model scenario a together with the class and write it on the board: Good decision: “I will check the weather report before the trip.” Bad decision: “I won’t check the weather report, I’ll just wear what I want.”
Choose some volunteer students to show the class how they could act out both the good and the bad decision in scenario a.

Put students in groups of three or four. Ask them to choose one of the scenes (e.g. before a test, walking home, at the lunch table, an online message) and discuss what the characters might be thinking about before they make their decision.
Then, choose a confident group to come to the front of the class and act out their scene, showing both the good and the bad decision.
After each scene, ask the class, “Which character made a good decision? Which character made a bad decision? Why?”
Ask other groups to come to the front and act out their scenes. Make sure every group acts out at least one or two of the scenes.
Ask students to look at activity B and ask some instruction-checking questions.
Put students into new groups of three or four and tell them that they should take turns asking and answering the questions so that all group members can say their answers.
Give about 6-8 minutes to discuss the questions.

Elicit ideas from each group. There are no real right or wrong answers, but answers should reflect the Teen Corner Value, e.g. “It is important to think before we act because our choices can help or hurt people.”

Wrap up the class by highlighting that we should think before we act, because good decisions help us stay safe, learn better, and be kind to others, just like checking the weather before choosing what to wear.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
